venues.d: A dawn convoy along the Andaman Trunk Road, then a speedboat through primeval mangrove creeks and a short forest walk to caves hung with stalactites and stalagmites: a proper adventure day out of Port Blair. The road crosses the protected Jarawa reserve in escorted convoy, where stopping, photography and any contact are strictly forbidden, and rightly so.

Small, bubbling cones of grey mud pushed up by natural gas: a rare geological curiosity and the other half of the classic Baratang day. Modest to look at but genuinely unusual, and a hit with children collecting oddities of nature.
The chilling British-built 1906 national memorial, where political prisoners were once held.

venues.d: The jungle-wreathed Victorian ruins of the colonial-era administrative headquarters, used until 1941.
Catch the sunrise at Kalapathar on Havelock, the most developed of the islands, with silky beaches backed by rainforest.
One of Asia's most spectacular beaches, for a stroll before dinner.
A flat, easy-going world of rice fields, palm trees and rocky beaches, with excellent diving.
